samples.summary: `Sheet.paste` returns `false` for a pivot sheet (`if (this.pivotDefinition) return false;`), and both views now treat `false` as "keep the copy buffer". Ctrl+C is not pivot-guarded in the view (only Ctrl+X is, packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:5089), so a copy on a pivot sheet followed by Ctrl+V leaves the buffer set forever — marching ants stay up and `isCutMode()`/`getCopyRange()` stay truthy (used by the overlay at packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:5557) until the user presses Escape. Before this delta the buffer was always cleared after a paste attempt. The pivot early return should be distinguished from a merge refusal (or the views should clear on non-merge refusals).

verdict.reason: All claimed evidence verified in-tree. `rangeOf` at packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:18-27 builds one array element per grid key and spreads it into `Math.min(...rows)`/`Math.max(...cols)`, which throws RangeError once the pasted grid exceeds the engine argument limit (~100k cells). It is called unconditionally on the paste path at sheet.ts:2255 and again from `selectPastedRange` at sheet.ts:2389 — the latter runs AFTER `this.store.endBatch()` (sheet.ts:2376) and before `return true` (2381), so the throw escapes `Sheet.paste` with the write already committed. No cell-count cap exists anywhere in packages/sheets/src/model (grep for MAX_/LIMIT yields only MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES at format.ts:14). Both view callers place their render after the awaited paste and absorb the throw in `console.error` (view/worksheet.ts:4904-4906; view/spreadsheet.ts:720-723), so the store is mutated but the grid is left unrendered and the selection stale, with no user-visible error. In-lane for blast-radius: the crash mechanism lives in a shared pre-existing helper consumed across the model and the silent-swallow impact is only visible at the two view call sites the diff does not show; the fix belongs in `rangeOf` (loop instead of spread). No ground for not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope.

finding.summary: Both UI paste paths call `clearCopyBuffer()` unconditionally, so the new "a refused paste leaves the buffer intact" behaviour never holds in the app
finding.evidence: `Worksheet.paste()` at packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4899-4901 does `await this.sheet!.paste({ text, html }); this.sheet!.clearCopyBuffer(); this.render();` and `Spreadsheet.paste()` at packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:715-718 does the same. The diff deliberately moved `if (isCut) this.copyBuffer = undefined;` after the merge-split guard (sheet.ts:2290-2295) so a refused paste keeps the cut buffer, and merge.test.ts:209 asserts `isCutMode() === true` after refusal — but through either real entry point the buffer is wiped a line later regardless. The user's cut is silently cancelled (marching ants vanish, nothing moved, no feedback), and a retry falls into the plain-TSV branch, losing formula relocation and merge propagation. The fix belongs in the view callers (only clear when the paste actually happened), or `paste()` must report refusal.

verdict.reason:
The finding claims both UI paste entry points call `clearCopyBuffer()` unconditionally after `sheet.paste(...)`. The repository shows the opposite: both call sites already gate the clear on the boolean return value of `paste()`.

- packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4899-4904 reads: "// A merged block can refuse the paste; keep the buffer so the marching ants stay up..." then `if (await this.sheet!.paste({ text, html })) { this.sheet!.clearCopyBuffer(); } this.render();` — not the claimed unconditional sequence.
- packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:715-720 is the identical guarded form: `if (await this.sheet.paste({ text, html })) { this.sheet.clearCopyBuffer(); }`.

`Sheet.paste()` is declared `Promise<boolean>` and documents returning false on refusal (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2165-2172, refusal returns at 2217, 2247, 2254, 2287), with the deferred cut clear at 2289-2291 — so the contract the callers depend on exists and is honoured.

An exhaustive grep of `clearCopyBuffer` yields only three production sites: worksheet.ts:4902 (guarded), spreadsheet.ts:718 (guarded), and worksheet.ts:5073-5075, which is the Escape-key handler (`if (this.sheet!.getCopyRange()) { this.sheet!.clearCopyBuffer(); }`) — an intentional user-initiated cancel, not a paste path. An exhaustive grep of `.paste(` shows no other production caller of `Sheet.paste()`: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx:758 goes through the guarded `Spreadsheet.paste()`, and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-context-menu.tsx:246 is the unrelated docs editor.

Therefore the described "buffer is wiped a line later regardless" code does not exist, and the refusal-preserves-buffer behaviour asserted at packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts:211-213 does hold through both real entry points.

finding.summary: `copyBuffer.merges` is a snapshot never invalidated by the other operations that mutate `this.merges`, so a later paste can re-create a block that no longer exists and silently clear destination cells under it
finding.evidence: `copy()`/`cut()` now snapshot `getMergesIntersecting(range)` into `copyBuffer` (sheet.ts:2153, 2173). Nothing invalidates that snapshot: `shiftCells` rewrites the merge map at sheet.ts:1320 (insert/delete rows/cols), `moveRows/moveColumns` at sheet.ts:1509, and `unmergeSelection` deletes blocks at sheet.ts:4540-4542 — none of them touch `copyBuffer` (`clearCopyBuffer` is only called from the views, packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4900/5071 and spreadsheet.ts:716). So: copy a merged range, unmerge it (or insert a row above it), then paste the still-matching clipboard text — `pastedMerges` re-creates the stale block at the destination and `clearCellsUnderMerge` (sheet.ts:927) deletes the destination cells it now covers. Previously the stale buffer could only mis-relocate formulas; it can now delete cell content and create merge geometry that never existed.

verdict.reason: The premise is false: there is no `copyBuffer.merges` snapshot to invalidate. `copyBuffer`'s type (sheet.ts:334-340) contains only `sourceRange`, `grid`, `rangeStyles`, `text`, `isCut`, and the only two assignments (`copy` at sheet.ts:2138, `cut` at sheet.ts:2151) do not call `getMergesIntersecting`. The internal-paste branch instead reads the merge layout LIVE at paste time (sheet.ts:2204, `const copiedMerges = this.getMergesIntersecting(sourceRange)`), with an explicit comment at sheet.ts:2201-2203 stating that a snapshot would survive `shiftCells`, `moveRows`/`moveColumns` and `unmergeSelection` and re-create a block that no longer exists. `pastedMerges` (sheet.ts:2221-2224) is derived from that live read, so after an unmerge or a merge-map shift the list is empty and no stale block is re-created and `clearCellsUnderMerge` never runs for it — the claimed data-loss path cannot occur. The reviewer's cited lines 2153/2173 are `cut`'s closing brace and `paste`'s pivot guard, not merge snapshots; the `copyBuffer.merges` wording comes from a stale plan doc (docs/tasks/active/20260822-sheet-paste-merge-propagation-todo.md:23-27) that the implementation deliberately diverged from. Stale `sourceRange` formula relocation remains, but the finding itself frames that as pre-existing, not the blocking claim.
